name: PT Indokripto Koin Semesta Tbk

frontmatter.title: Indokripto Koin Semesta — a licensed crypto exchange priced for a franchise it does not yet earn
frontmatter.summary: COIN owns the first OJK-licensed Indonesian crypto exchange and its custodian, but the equity is large, the earnings base has halved, and returns sit far below the cost of equity. We initiate at SELL with a target well below the market price, which discounts a recovery the current cost base cannot deliver.
thesis: SELL: the shares trade at several times book value for a business earning a low-single-digit return on equity, while our justified P/B valuation points to a fraction of book.
The 2026 revenue collapse is booked, not hypothetical: nine-month revenue roughly halved and the company swung to a net loss as spot crypto activity fell.
The derivative segment is the one genuine growth engine, but it is still small relative to the cost base and to the equity the company raised.
Governance and market-structure overhangs — special-monitoring board status, repeated suspensions and the MSCI review — keep the cost of equity high and institutional demand thin.
The balance sheet is liquid and the licence is real, so the bear case is a value trap rather than a solvency event; the bull case needs derivative scale we do not yet see in the numbers.

catalysts.event: FY2026 audited results — first full-year loss and the cost-base response
MSCI consultation on Indonesia market classification closes
MSCI final decision on Indonesia classification
IDX special-monitoring board review and monthly OJK crypto transaction data

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Indokripto Koin Semesta Tbk (COIN) at **SELL** with a target of Rp31, implying a return of -92.1% from the Rp394 share price. The company is the listed holding vehicle for PT Central Finansial X (CFX), the first Indonesian crypto asset exchange licensed and supervised by OJK, and for PT Kustodian Koin Indonesia (ICC), a licensed crypto custodian [S2]. That licence is a genuine franchise asset, but the equity around it is large, the earnings are small and volatile, and the shares price a recovery that the current cost base does not support.

*Revision note — first review round.* The target falls from our prior single-method number because the valuation now blends a residual-income leg (25% weight) with the justified-P/B multiple, and because the cost-of-equity build, the book base and the cash position are now disclosed line by line in the valuation section. The rating is unchanged. The residual-income leg values the same franchise off its profit path and lands materially below the multiple, so adding it removes the single-method weakness the red team identified rather than softening the call.

Our variant view is simple. The market is paying 3.7x book value for a company whose FY2025 return on equity was 3.8% and whose nine-month 2026 result was a net loss of 40.8 IDR bn [S4]. A financial holding with a low-single-digit return on equity, a 11.9% cost of equity and modest terminal growth is worth a fraction of book on a justified P/B basis; we compute 0.3x book, or Rp30 per share before the roll-forward [S4][S6]. The three things that move the value are the trajectory of crypto spot and derivative volumes, the company's ability to cut the cost base to the smaller revenue pool, and whether the governance overhang around the listing status ever clears [S4][S12].

The bear and bull cases are deliberately narrow. Both keep the licence and the custodian inside the value; they differ on how fast derivative revenue scales and on the risk premium the market assigns to a special-monitoring-board name [S6][S13]. Even the bull case does not approach today's price, which is why the asymmetry sits on the downside.

COIN is the listed holding company form that Indonesian exchanges and custodians have adopted since the sector moved under OJK supervision. Its economics are those of a regulated venue: transaction and service fees on client activity, a fixed compliance and technology cost base, and capital held against a licensed entity. The licence is the scarce asset; the earnings follow market activity.

COIN is an investment holding company founded to own and govern crypto-market infrastructure in Indonesia. Its two operating subsidiaries are CFX, which operates a crypto asset exchange, and ICC, which provides crypto asset custody; the company also describes commodity physical-trading intermediary and software/IT services within the group [S2][S3]. The group is headquartered at CFX Tower in South Jakarta and is small in headcount relative to its market capitalisation, with 104.0 employees reported in the data pack [S0].

The revenue model is volume-linked rather than subscription-like. Exchange and custodian fees rise and fall with client trading activity, so the P&L is a leveraged play on crypto turnover. The segment disclosure bears this out: derivative products have become the growth engine, contributing 36.7% of revenue in the nine months to September 2026 against a much smaller share a year earlier, and reaching 48.1% of revenue in the third quarter alone [S4][S6]. Spot-related revenue, by contrast, contracted with the market.

The strategy is to broaden the product set beyond spot trading. Management argues that only a minority of CFX's members currently offer derivative services to their clients, so distribution of derivative products through member brokers is the identified growth runway [S4][S6]. The custodian subsidiary is intended to capture the custody and safekeeping economics that sit alongside trading. The company raised public equity at listing and had used only 24.0% of the IPO proceeds a year later, which tells us the build-out is slow relative to the capital raised [S4].

Competitively, COIN is a first mover with a sole licence rather than a scale leader. CFX is described by the company as the first and only Indonesian crypto exchange licensed and supervised by OJK — a single licensed venue, not one of several, and that sole licence is the franchise [S2]. What it does not confer is pricing power: the group's revenue of IDR284.8bn in FY2025 is small in absolute terms, and the competitive constraint comes from offshore and unregulated channels rather than from a domestic rival [S0][S3]. Its differentiator is the combination of the sole exchange licence plus the custodian under one listed holding company.

Ownership is concentrated. The Arsari Group of Hashim Djojohadikusumo became a shareholder in late 2025, a transaction the company presented as strengthening governance and corporate scale [S9]. The data pack reports insider ownership of 85.0% against a free float of 43.1% from the IDX-IC registry [S0]; those two figures cannot both be right, and we treat the free-float series as approximate until the shareholder register is reconciled. The board was reshuffled at an extraordinary general meeting in June 2026, with a commissioner replaced [S14].

The group structure matters for the valuation. COIN is not an operating exchange with a controlling family overlay; it is a holding company whose value is the sum of a licensed exchange, a custodian and a cash-rich but low-return balance sheet. We value it on consolidated equity and returns rather than on a sum of listed stakes, because neither subsidiary is separately listed [S2][S3].

Indonesia's crypto market is regulated, large in user count and violently cyclical in value. OJK reported crypto asset transaction value of 30,560 IDR bn in September 2026, up sharply month on month, with 23.5 m accounts registered digital-asset consumer accounts [S11]. Derivative transactions reached 5,800 IDR bn in the same month, growing at a double-digit monthly rate [S11]. The user base and the derivative line are the structural positives; the spot turnover is the cyclical swing factor that has hurt COIN's revenue [S4][S6].

The market's direction in 2026 has been down at the aggregate level even as derivatives grew. COIN's own disclosure shows nine-month revenue falling by roughly half, with the third quarter at 31.4 IDR bn [S6]. That is consistent with a market where spot activity normalised sharply after a strong prior year while derivative volumes held up better. The implication for the industry is that venues with derivative and custody capabilities are more resilient than pure spot exchanges, but none of them is immune to a revenue swing of the size COIN has just absorbed [S6].

Regulation is the defining competitive force. OJK supervises crypto assets and the exchanges, and CFX's licence is the barrier that keeps the number of venues small [S2]. The same regulator publishes monthly transaction and account data, which gives us a high-frequency read on the industry and on COIN's addressable activity [S11]. Compliance costs are fixed and non-negotiable, which is why the cost base did not fall as fast as revenue in 2026.

Competitive positioning is best described as a sole-licence operator with a product gap. CFX holds the only OJK crypto-exchange licence in the country [S2], and management itself frames the opportunity as extending derivative access to the member brokers that do not yet offer it [S4][S6]. That is a distribution problem more than a technology problem, and it is the right thing for the company to be solving. But the addressable revenue pool is COIN's own small fee take, not the trillion-rupiah transaction values passing through the venue.

The five forces are mixed. Supplier power is low: technology and compliance inputs are available to any licensed venue. Buyer power is moderate: member brokers and large traders can route activity to the substitutes, and the monthly data shows how quickly volumes move. Threat of new entrants is contained by the sole licence and by OJK supervision, which is a genuine structural positive we have to weigh against the current numbers. Substitutes are real and are the live competitive threat: offshore venues and unregulated channels still compete for Indonesian users, even if the regulated share is rising. Rivalry among domestic venues is therefore limited, but rivalry for the user is not, and fee compression is a permanent feature [S2][S3][S6].

Market structure is an additional external force. MSCI has proposed reclassifying Indonesia to Standalone Market status, with a consultation running to April 2027 and a final decision due by June 2027; the review explicitly cites concerns about ownership transparency and coordinated trading [S7]. For a small-cap with a concentrated register and a special-monitoring-board history, that process is a direct risk to the investor base, not a distant macro issue [S7][S12].

The Indonesian crypto market moved from commodity-futures supervision to the financial-services regulator as the asset class was reclassified under the financial sector. That transition is why the venue licence, the custodian licence and the monthly regulatory data release all sit with the same authority. The practical effect for listed venues is that compliance and reporting obligations rose while the fee pool remained tied to trading activity.

FY2025 was a good year that flattered the return on equity. Revenue reached IDR284.8bn, net profit to parent was IDR49.1bn, and parent equity stood at IDR1,550.4bn, or Rp105 per share [S0]. On opening equity that is a return of 3.8% — respectable for a young venue but low against the cost of equity we apply. No dividend was paid, and the payout ratio was 0.0% [S0].

The 2026 numbers are the reason the thesis changed. Revenue for the nine months to September fell to 105 IDR bn from 205 IDR bn a year earlier, a contraction of roughly half, and the company reported a net loss of 40.8 IDR bn against a profit of 25.5 IDR bn in the comparable period [S4][S6]. The third quarter alone produced revenue of 31.4 IDR bn, meaning the run-rate exiting the period is far below the FY2025 average [S6]. Our FY2026E revenue is IDR135.8bn, a sourced decline rather than a cautious haircut, because most of it is already booked.

The cost base is the swing factor for 2027. Compliance, technology and people costs did not halve with revenue, so the company moved from a double-digit net margin in FY2025 to a loss in 2026 [S0][S4]. Our forecast assumes management takes cost out through 2027 and that derivative revenue keeps compounding from a small base; on that path FY2026E net profit to parent is IDR-60.5bn and the return on equity is -3.9%, recovering to 6.0% by FY2030E as the mix shifts toward derivatives [S4][S6]. That recovery is the single most important assumption in the model, and it is deliberately gradual. The mix shift is the only lever that matters at this scale: with a cost base that is largely fixed in the near term, each rupiah of derivative fee revenue drops through at a higher margin than the spot revenue it replaces, which is why the FY2030E ROE recovery is a mix story rather than a volume story [S4][S6].

Cash and gearing are not the problem. The group carries more cash than debt — a net cash position on the 30 September 2026 balance sheet — so the 2026 loss is an earnings event, not a liquidity event [S0]. Capital allocation is the weakness: the listing raised equity that has been slow to deploy, with only 24.0% of IPO proceeds used a year after listing, and the cash sits on the balance sheet earning a deposit yield rather than compounding in the business [S4]. That is why the equity base stayed large while profit fell.

Earnings quality needs flagging rather than glossing. Cash conversion has been volatile across the cycle, with operating cash flow swinging from negative in FY2024 to comfortably above net profit in FY2025 and back to an outflow in the last twelve months [S0]. A financial holding with negative operating cash flow and a reported loss is not manipulating accruals — the loss is real and cash-backed — but it does mean the quality of any future profit recovery depends on revenue, not on working-capital releases. We also note that the balance-sheet date is 30 September 2026, so the numbers are pre-Q4 and pre any year-end true-ups.

The regime flags are the most important item in this section, and they need dating. COIN was suspended more than once in August 2025 and was placed on the IDX special monitoring board (papan pemantauan khusus, full call auction) on 24 July 2025 and again from 1 September 2025, when the suspension in force since 26 August 2025 was lifted; the stock was also the subject of an unusual market activity announcement [S8][S12][S13]. That is where our evidence ends: the last confirmation we hold is the 29 August 2025 announcement effective 1 September 2025, and we have not verified the board status after September 2026. We therefore describe the regime as an established 2025 history rather than a confirmed present state — every statement in this report that relies on it is qualified to that date, and the next dated check is the catalyst we carry in the monitoring section [S12][S13].

We value COIN on justified price-to-book, with residual income as a second, independent method. The method set fits because this is a financial holding with an equity-heavy balance sheet, negative or highly volatile earnings and no dividend [S0][S4]. Justified P/B ties the value to the two things we can observe — book value and the return earned on it — and penalises a company that earns less than its cost of equity. Residual income discounts the forecast profit path against the same cost of equity and charges the loss years explicitly, so the answer does not depend on a blanket book multiple. Earnings-based cross-checks are not available: the FY2026E denominator is negative, the FY2025A multiple of 118.1x is a flotation artefact on a tiny earnings base rather than a benchmark, and a dividend-discount model returns zero because the payout is zero [S0]. We say that rather than average in a meaningless number.

The cost-of-equity build is line by line: a risk-free rate of 7.4%, less the Indonesian sovereign default spread of 1.6% that the engine deducts so that country risk is not counted twice, plus a beta of 0.90 times the sum of the mature-market equity risk premium (4.2%) and the country risk premium (2.5%), which gives 11.9%. The engine fixes D/E at 0.00 for financial-equity templates by construction, so beta is not relevered for the group's net cash: we accept that convention because cash is an asset, not negative operating leverage, and relevering on a negative D/E would mechanically lower the hurdle and raise the target. The 11.9% cost of equity is the rate applied to both methods.

The primary input is a normalised sustainable return on equity of 6.0%. We state plainly what that number is: it is the FY2030E forecast input and the long-run value, not a midpoint between the FY2025A outcome of 3.8% and the horizon. With terminal growth of 3.5% and a cost of equity of 11.9%, the justified P/B is 0.3x. Applied to the book value per share on the 30 September 2026 balance sheet — the base the engine uses, not the FY2025A figure of Rp105, which we show for reference only — that gives Rp30 per share [S0][S4].

The target convention is disclosed because it matters: the pre-roll value is grossed up one year at the cost of equity less dividend per share expected within twelve months (Rp0), taking Rp26 to a base-case target of Rp29. That is the required return on holding the equity, not evidence of a re-rating; a book grown at the retained return on equity instead would add materially less. The dated catalysts that could justify paying a year of return inside the twelve months are the FY2026 audited results in February 2027, the MSCI consultation close in April 2027 and the next IDX special-monitoring-board review [S4][S7][S12].

The financial-equity template carries no sum-of-the-parts method, and no registered source marks CFX or ICC separately, so we cannot split the three parts of this company into separate cards [S2][S3]. We flag what consolidating them costs rather than let it pass silently: the 0.3x multiple marks the net cash on the 30 September 2026 balance sheet — roughly a fifth of book equity — at the same discount as the operating franchises, although cash is worth face, and it marks the sole exchange licence and the custodian at that same multiple. The direction of that error is up — lifting net cash out at face would raise the target by roughly the cash's share of book — and we disclose the conservatism instead of modelling an SOTP the template cannot carry.

The residual-income leg lands at Rp13 against Rp30 for the multiple, a divergence of -58.0%, and we accept it rather than force agreement. The reason is mechanical and visible: residual income charges every forecast year at the 11.9% hurdle, so the FY2026E loss and the near-zero returns through FY2028E are charged in full, while the P/B method compresses them into one sustainable-ROE override. Together the two methods bracket a value well below the market price, which is the point of showing both.

The ROE path is explicit rather than asserted: -3.9% in FY2026E, 0.5% in FY2027E, 2.5%, 4.5% and 6.0% in FY2030E, driven by the derivative share of revenue rising to 36.7% of the nine-month total while only a minority of CFX members yet offer derivative products [S4][S6]. The long-run margin that the path implies — FY2035E profit of IDR128.8bn on revenue of IDR342.1bn — is not a margin call we sourced: it is the arithmetic of equity compounding at the retained ROE with no dividend while revenue grows at the slower revenue-growth assumption. That makes the margin expansion the weakest link in the forecast, and it is the first thing the bear case attacks [S0][S4].

The economics of the sustainable-ROE assumption are worth stating because the target is sensitive to it: the justified multiple is (ROE − g)/(COE − g), so a sustainable ROE at the bottom of our bear path compresses the target towards zero, while one at the bull path would more than double it. The engine exposes no sustainable-ROE axis in its sensitivity grid, and its ROE override is inert to scenario shocks (disclosed with the scenarios), so we do not dress that sensitivity up as an engine output. It is the single assumption a reader should stress hardest.

What the price implies is the cleanest way to state the variant view. At Rp394 the market is capitalising COIN at IDR5,794.1bn, or 3.7x the FY2025A book value, for a business that earned 3.8% on equity in its last profitable year and lost money in the current one [S0][S4]. To justify that multiple on a justified P/B framework, the sustainable return on equity would need to approach the cost of equity; our forecast reaches 6.0% only at the end of the horizon. The gap is the short case.

The twelve-month range tells its own story: Rp4,610 at the peak against Rp256 at the trough, with the shares now at Rp394 [S0]. We do not anchor on either extreme. The valuation is built from book value, the return on it and the cost of equity, and it lands far below the market price because the company's returns are far below its cost of capital.

The downside risks are specific and, in our view, underappreciated by the price. First, market-structure risk: the special monitoring board and repeated suspensions restrict trading and keep institutional money away, and the MSCI review cites ownership transparency and coordinated-trading concerns for the Indonesian market as a whole [S7][S12][S13]. Likelihood high, impact high. Second, earnings risk: the revenue run-rate has halved and the fixed compliance cost base has not, so a further leg down in crypto activity pushes the loss deeper and delays the ROE recovery [S4][S6]. Likelihood medium, impact high.

Third, governance risk: a concentrated register, a board reshuffle and a new strategic shareholder create the conditions for related-party or control transactions that minority holders cannot block [S9][S14]. Likelihood medium, impact high. Fourth, liquidity risk: three-month average traded value was IDR36.4bn a day against a market capitalisation of IDR5,794.1bn, so the engine's liquidity-discount table returns 0.0 and we do not apply a discount; the caveat is that the register cannot be reconciled — the data pack reports insider ownership of 85.0% against a free float of 43.1%, which cannot both be true, so the true float is unverified and the pack's ADTV covers the suspension-distorted period [S0][S12]. Exit at the screen price is accordingly less assured than the turnover number implies, and that is a risk we carry in the narrative rather than in a discount we cannot source. Likelihood medium, impact high. Fifth, commodity-cycle risk: crypto volumes are the revenue driver and they are not forecastable with confidence [S11]. Likelihood high, impact medium. Currency risk is minor because revenue and costs are domestic.

Two risks sit outside those five. The first is equity overhang: the listing raised capital that is still largely undeployed — only 24.0% of IPO proceeds had been used a year later — and a company funding a fixed cost base from a shrinking revenue pool is the kind of issuer that returns to shareholders for more capital; a discounted rights issue would dilute the per-share book value on which our valuation rests [S4]. The second is disclosure risk: the shareholder register in the data pack is internally inconsistent on insider and free-float percentages, the auditor's opinion is not in our registered sources, and related-party flows are not quantifiable from the disclosures we hold [S0][S9]. We treat both as reasons to hold the cost of equity where it is rather than as separate valuation lines. The scenario spread is correspondingly narrow: even the bull case values the equity well below the market price, so the asymmetry that matters is between our base case and the price, not between our own scenarios [S4][S6].

The scenarios mirror the same drivers. In the bear case, spot volumes stay depressed, the cost base is slow to adjust and the risk premium stays elevated, so we raise the cost of equity; in the bull case, derivative distribution across CFX members scales, spot normalises and the risk premium narrows, so we lower it by the same amount. Both tails also shock the ROE path by the same three percentage points in opposite directions, which is what the bull case is really about: derivative revenue reaching enough of the member base to lift the return on equity above the base-case path. That shock is not inert in the residual-income leg or in book value, because both run off the profit path; it is inert in the justified P/B leg, whose sustainable-ROE override is fixed, so that leg is unchanged between states. We disclose the mechanic rather than present a false ROE sensitivity in the multiple [S4][S6]. Probabilities put half the weight on the base case and split the rest evenly between the tails, consistent with a base case that assumes a gradual, not a V-shaped, recovery [S4][S6].

The signposts that would change our view are concrete. A sustained rise in the derivative share of revenue with a stable cost base would lift the sustainable ROE and therefore the justified multiple [S6]. A resumption of spot turnover growth in the monthly OJK data would do the same [S11]. Removal from the special monitoring board and an end to suspensions would lower the risk premium [S12][S13]. Conversely, a further revenue decline, a rights issue or a related-party transaction at less than fair value would push us further down the bear path [S9][S14].

Ownership and control are concentrated and have changed. The Arsari Group became a shareholder in late 2025, presented by the company as a governance and scale enhancement [S9]. The data pack reports insider ownership of 85.0%, which with a reported free float of 43.1% is internally inconsistent; we flag the register as a data-quality issue and do not rely on the free-float figure for index or liquidity work [S0]. The practical point is that minority holders have limited influence over control transactions.

Board and management changes have been frequent for a company of this size. An extraordinary general meeting in June 2026 approved a commissioner's resignation and appointed a replacement, and the company maintains audit and nomination/remuneration committees [S2][S14]. Frequent board churn in a small cap with a concentrated register is a governance watch item, not a disqualifier, but it adds to the risk premium. We found no evidence of pledged controlling shares in the sources reviewed; that is an absence of evidence, not a clean bill of health.

The IDX regime flags are the dominant governance fact, with a date attached. COIN was suspended more than once in August 2025, was moved to the special monitoring board (papan pemantauan khusus) in July and again from September 2025, and has had an unusual market activity announcement [S8][S12][S13]. Under the house earnings-quality screen that is an investability gate: full call auction, restricted entry and exit, and a shareholder base that cannot rely on continuous trading. We classify it as an optics-and-structure flag rather than a proven manipulation-class flag, because the disclosures are public and the company has continued to report [S12][S13]. Our last dated confirmation of the board status is September 2025; we have not verified it in November 2026, and we flag that gap here and with the scenarios rather than assert a present-tense fact we have not sourced.

On capital allocation, the dividend record is empty and we do not forecast one; the company retains everything for the build-out [S0]. We could not verify the auditor or the audit opinion from the registered sources, so we do not opine on it — that is a gap in our evidence, not a finding. Related-party flows are not disclosed in enough detail in the sources we hold to quantify them as a share of revenue, and we say so rather than estimate.

ESG exposure is concentrated in the sector's own issues. Crypto venues carry anti-money-laundering and know-your-customer obligations, custody and consumer-protection risk, and energy-use scrutiny; OJK supervision and the custodian licence internalise much of that, and the monthly regulatory data release gives a public read on account growth and transaction activity [S11]. The company's governance disclosures emphasise committees and transparency, but the market-structure concerns raised in the MSCI review are the more material ESG-adjacent issue for investors [S7].

The dated catalysts are the FY2026 audited results, expected early in 2027, which will show the first full-year loss and management's cost response [S4]. The MSCI consultation closes at the end of April 2027, with a final decision due by the end of June 2027; a downgrade to Standalone Market status would hit the whole small-cap complex, and COIN's concentrated register makes it more exposed than most [S7]. On the IDX side, the first dated item is the missing one: we carry the board status as unverified after September 2025, so any current confirmation of the special monitoring board, or a further suspension, is a live catalyst in either direction [S12][S13].

Between updates we monitor a short list of KPIs. The derivative share of revenue is the first: if it keeps rising while total revenue stabilises, the recovery is real [S6]. Monthly OJK data on crypto transaction value and PAKD accounts is the second, because it leads COIN's fee revenue [S11]. The third is the cost base: operating expenses relative to the smaller revenue pool determine whether 2027 is a recovery year or another loss year [S0][S4]. We also watch the share register, any rights issue and any related-party transaction, given the concentration of control [S9][S14].

The rating is a SELL because the price discounts a franchise outcome that the numbers do not yet support. The licence, the custodian and the liquid balance sheet are real assets and they belong in the valuation; they are worth a fraction of book on the returns the company currently earns, and the gap to the market price is the trade [S0][S4].

bear.narrative: Crypto spot volumes stay depressed, the special-monitoring board keeps institutions out, and the cost of equity stays elevated; ROE recovers two years later and the justified P/B compresses.

bull.narrative: Derivative products scale across CFX members and the custodian, spot volumes normalise, ROE reaches 6% sooner and the risk premium narrows as governance concerns fade.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs ROE and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E -52.3%: 9M-2026 revenue Rp105.17bn (-48.6% yoy) plus a Q4 at the Q3 run-rate of Rp31.39bn [S6]; recovery from FY2027E as derivative revenue scales (36.7% of 9M revenue vs 20.1%) [S6]

assumptions.label: ROE on opening equity
assumptions.basis: FY2026E -3.9%: 9M-2026 net loss Rp40.78bn [S4] on opening equity Rp1,550bn; recovery to 6.0% by FY2030E as the derivative mix rises from 20.1% to 36.7% of revenue and CFX adds derivative members [S4][S6]

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2025A minorities were Rp0.006bn of Rp49.05bn net profit (0.01%); the engine history average is distorted by the 2023 minority loss, so hold at zero [S0]

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: COIN has never paid a dividend: dps_ttm is zero and the data pack has no dividend record since listing; all earnings retained for the exchange and custodian build-out [S0]

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Share count is stable at 14,705.9m with no splits in the pack history; no rights issue announced in the sources reviewed

assumptions.label: Terminal growth
assumptions.basis: 3.5% nominal: domestic crypto transaction value rose 31.96% m/m in September 2026 and PAKD accounts reached 23.51m, but a regulated exchange franchise matures with nominal GDP rather than compounding [S11]

challenges.challenge: The bear and bull shocks target a.roe, but the justified P/B reads valuation.roe_sustainable (override 0.06 in fund record _sustainable_roe), which no scenario changes; bear 31 and bull 38 are produced solely by val.coe +/-1pp. Had the ROE shock landed, bear ROE 3% with g 3.5% gives a negative justified P/B (value floored at zero), so the 25% bear weight and the 34 probability-weighted target do not describe the model that ran.

findings.finding: The calibration.roe justification says the Q3 loss of about Rp14.8bn (9M -40.78 less F13 1H -26.0) is the number the quarterly run-rate uses, but FY2026E np_parent of -60.47 implies a Q4 loss of -19.7bn, a third worse than that run-rate with revenue held flat; FY2026E revenue of 135.83 is likewise 0.5pct below the stated 105.17 + 31.39 build.

Section 4 asserts the consolidated multiple is conservative because lifting the Rp309bn net cash out at face would raise the target by roughly the cash share of book (20.7pct). On the report own 0.296x, cash at face adds 0.7 x Rp308.9bn = Rp14.7/share, about +48pct on the Rp30 leg, and the ROE already capitalises the deposit yield the cash earns, so face value is not established.

The RI terminal value applies g of 3.5pct to FY2035 residual income while payout is 0.0pct and ROE 6.0pct, so equity and residual income compound at 6pct; a consistent terminal would take the Rp13 leg to about zero or below. The leg therefore overstates rather than understates value, so the 25pct weight raises the target.

C8 rebuttal accepted: the discount is engine-set from the Rp36.4bn ADTV against house thresholds, the analyst cannot type it, and section 5 discloses the unreconciled register and the suspension-distorted ADTV window. But the pack ADTV is 0.63pct of market cap a day for an FCA-traded stock with an 85pct insider register, so the 0pct point is not evidence of liquidity.

The drift.roe justification mix ratio of 20.1pct to 36.7pct of revenue is a denominator effect: 9M derivative revenue is 0.367 x 105.17 = Rp38.6bn against 0.201 x 204.63 = Rp41.1bn a year earlier, down 6pct yoy (F10, F1, F2). The forward ROE recovery rests on the sourced 6-of-21 CFX member distribution runway, not on derivative growth already booked.
